title: The night the stars fell over America ☄️
subject: meteor
description:
Would you have thought the world was ending? 👇

On November 12–13, 1833, the Leonid meteor storm filled the sky over North America with more than 100,000 meteors an hour at its peak. The Leonids peak again this month, around November 17.

Sources: Wikipedia (Leonids; NASA Leonid MAC history), Smithsonian Magazine (2024), Denison Olmsted, American Journal of Science and Arts (1834)

scenes.text: For nine hours, the sky rained shooting stars.
It was November 13, 1833, and it was seen from Canada to Jamaica.
One Boston paper said meteor followed meteor so fast it was "impossible to count them." Estimates put the peak above 100,000 an hour.
At Yale, Denison Olmsted traced every streak to one point in the constellation Leo, beyond our atmosphere.
The Leonids return every November, and about every 33 years they can storm again. In 1966, observers saw over 40 a second.
